clue.text: Firmly convinced a chap each inset is specially tailored

indicators.note: inset says the following pieces are set into the phrase that comes before them

parts.note: to have made sure of something is to have become firmly convinced of it
Tom is any man's name, so a chap
EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price lists

explanation.surface: A man who is firmly convinced that each chap's suit is bespoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inset' signals the container; the 'a' before chap is only a link, giving no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes cut to a customer's own measurements are bespoke, made individually for that person.

clue.text: Making fast, low metallic sound

parts.note: to low is the noise a cow makes, so a moo
a ring is the sound of a bell or struck metal

explanation.surface: A deep metallic note rings out as something is fastened quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying up a boat to a quay or buoy is securing it, making it fast.

clue.text: Go after girl having initially suffered neglect

indicators.note: after says the piece for Go comes behind the girl and her companion letter

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of suffered

parts.note: to repair to a place is to go there

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a girl who has suffered neglect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb of chasing, but it is REPAIR in its old sense of going somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in poor condition through lack of upkeep has been neglected; the noun names that state.

clue.text: He's left the noisy rabble for a bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: left means the letters of He have departed, been taken out of the phrase

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a disorderly, noisy crowd
taken as written: the letters of He, with 's meaning has

explanation.surface: A man abandons the rowdy mob in favour of a grumpy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' takes HE out of THE ROUT, the 'the' being part of the fodder rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Old trout is British slang for an ill-tempered or unpleasant older woman.

clue.text: Fellow soldier's hash, served on china

indicators.note: in a down clue, served on says the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a hash is a mess, a muddle
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A soldier's comrade has his stew dished up on a porcelain plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade who eats in the same military mess is a fellow member of that unit.

clue.text: A crazy article about Rodney's first fleet

indicators.note: about says the opening pieces go round the letter taken from Rodney

parts.note: crazy means mad
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of Rodney

explanation.surface: Admiral Rodney's first fleet described in a wild newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Rodney was a famous British naval commander, which makes 'fleet' look like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a large fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Likely to put out musical version of poem after going to city

indicators.note: after says the musical piece follows the piece for going to the city

parts.note: in British usage one goes up to London or a university city
a setting is music composed for a poem's words

explanation.surface: A composer's song version of a poem is disturbing once it reaches the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Travelling 'up' to London is a British convention, whichever direction the journey actually goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distressing tends to disturb or annoy people, putting them out.

clue.text: Incident involving archdeacon in popular film

indicators.note: in says the archdeacon's abbreviation goes inside the film title

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's hit film about an alien
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A scandal involving a senior clergyman appears in a blockbuster film.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or happening, something that takes place.

clue.text: Promise made leading characters in play nervous?

parts.note: the first two letters of play
to be on edge is to be nervous; the question mark flags that the first pair is put on the edge

explanation.surface: A vow that made the stars of a show anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made ... nervous' is read as 'put on edge': in a down clue PL is placed on EDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn undertaking or vow to do something.

clue.text: Bony host uses house — just the central parts

indicators.note: just the central parts says to drop the first and last letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A thin landlord makes use of his house.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outside letters of host, uses and house to leave OS, SE and OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of or resembling skeleton tissue; osseous is the technical word.

clue.text: Faulty distribution Kent beauty queen reported

indicators.note: reported says the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a beauty queen from Deal, a town in Kent, would be crowned Miss Deal

explanation.surface: News of a crooked handout by a beauty queen from Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a seaside town in Kent, so its beauty queen is Miss Deal.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, dealing the cards wrongly is a botched share-out.

clue.text: Backing one writing in Italian is awkward

indicators.note: in says the reversed writing tool goes inside the abbreviation for Italian

parts.note: IT is a short form of Italian, as in gin and it

indicators.note: Backing says the word pen is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a pen is one thing used in writing

explanation.surface: Supporting a single Italian writer turns out clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like support, but it turns the pen round before 'in' sets it inside the Italian abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy or lacking skill, as a gauche or incompetent person is.

clue.text: About to make amendments, dull press chief pondered

indicators.note: About says the word for dull goes round the word for making amendments

parts.note: mat is a spelling of matt, meaning not shiny
to edit is to make amendments to a text
ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tired newspaper editor thought hard before making his corrections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' opens the clue as if meaning 'on the point of', but it is the container signal; mat is a variant spelling of matt.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought deeply about, considered at length.

clue.text: Fair gift for making scribblings in public?

indicators.note: making says the letters of the two words are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A fine present inspiring people to write on walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition of wall writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Words or drawings scrawled on walls in public places.

clue.text: Unprofitable, having no dates, perhaps

definitions.meaning: producing no useful result or gain
dates are one kind of produce from a tree, so lacking them means being without that crop

explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says dates are just one example of the produce missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A futile effort bears no fruit, a crop metaphor for gaining nothing.

clue.text: Limited penalty demanded for pinching wine

indicators.note: for pinching says the penalty word grips the wine word inside it

parts.note: a fine is a money penalty demanded of an offender
it is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A capped fine imposed on someone for stealing wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' for Italian vermouth is an old bar abbreviation, as in gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having bounds or an end, not infinite.

clue.text: He loves to roam in a maze

indicators.note: in a maze means bewildered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man who loves to wander through a labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' belongs to the fodder; 'maze' alone tells us to scramble TO ROAM IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian loanword for a male lover, someone who adores another.

clue.text: Lazy person had draught of liquor on state highway

indicators.note: in a down clue, on says the drink sits above the next pieces

parts.note: a slug is a swig of spirits
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An idle man takes a swig of whisky by the interstate.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitually idle person, a slacker.

clue.text: Impecunious firm has spell of prosperity

parts.note: firm means hard, solid
an up is a good time, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: A company enjoys a boom period.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests wealth, but the answer means the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Short of money, poor.

clue.text: Posh brother, secure in his pride

indicators.note: secure in says the first pieces are locked inside his

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A well-to-do brother is confident in his own pride.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British convention from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive arrogance or overweening self-confidence, a Greek idea.

clue.text: Glaring old woman in self-contained accommodation

indicators.note: in says the old woman goes inside the accommodation

parts.note: a flat is a self-contained set of rooms
gran is grandmother, an old woman

explanation.surface: A grandmother glares from her own apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspicuous and shocking, as an obvious offence is.

clue.text: Petty quarrel over some gauzy fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the quarrel sits above the next word

parts.note: a tiff is a minor row
any means some, as in have you any?

explanation.surface: A minor row breaks out over a scrap of sheer material.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, transparent muslin or silk gauze.

clue.text: Greeting shouted in our direction in break?

parts.note: hi is a greeting called out
aimed at us, towards ourselves

explanation.surface: Someone yells hello to us during an interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shouted' hints at a sound-alike, but the letters are simply a greeting plus 'at us'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap or pause in continuity.

clue.text: Respiration could be rough for Hellenes

definitions.meaning: the taking in and letting out of air
in ancient Greek script, a rough mark over an opening vowel shows an h sound

explanation.walkthrough: Greek writing has rough and smooth diacritics on initial vowels; the rough one adds an h sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing air in and out of the lungs is the act of respiring.

clue.text: Some, men do well to provide permanent finance for …

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some men do well enough to fund things permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a permanent income, as a benefactor does to a college.

clue.text: Skilled pilot originally given money for take-off

indicators.note: originally tells us to take the opening letters of Skilled and pilot

parts.note: oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: An expert flyer is paid to handle the take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' looks like aviation but means a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody or send-up, imitating something to mock it.

clue.text: … holidays taken at first in States

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for states

parts.note: to state something is to say it

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of taken

explanation.surface: Breaks are first taken in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like America, but it is the verb, SAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Visits or periods spent away, as hotel stays are.

clue.text: Ten wild characters reformed and lived in

indicators.note: the letters (characters) of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten wild people changed their ways and settled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters reformed' asks for the letters of TEN WILD rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Resided in or occupied; often of a spirit inhabiting someone.

clue.text: Source of cotton woman used to bind Arab garment

indicators.note: used to bind says the woman's name wraps round the garment

parts.note: Alma is a woman's name
an aba is a loose sleeveless Arab robe

explanation.surface: A woman wraps an Arab robe made of cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to bind' looks like a past habit, but here it means the woman is used to wrap the robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Deep South, historically a major cotton-growing region.

clue.text: Musical bridge-player goes along with politician

parts.note: West is one of the four players at bridge
sides with means supports, goes along with
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A card player agrees with a Conservative MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points; Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bernstein stage show set in New York's gangland.
